                    ### Question
                    A 25-year-old woman presented to an urgent care center with a complaint of a cough for more than 3 weeks that was accompanied by night sweats, weight loss, and malaise. On physical examination, the patient had slightly pale palpebral conjunctivae bilateral posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, but with no adventitious breath sounds in the lung fields bilaterally. The remainder of the physical examination was routine. The patient was started on a drug regimen that was to be taken for 6 months. On follow-up after 2 months, the ALT and AST levels were elevated. Which of the following anti-tubercular drug could have contributed to this labor result?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Rifampicin
opb. Pyrazinamide
opc. Isoniazid
opd. Streptomycin
ope. Ethambutol

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the context of anti-tubercular treatment, both isoniazid and pyrazinamide are known to cause hepatotoxicity, which can lead to elevated ALT and AST levels. Isoniazid is particularly noted for this side effect and aligns with the medical consensus as a common cause of drug-induced liver injury. Pyrazinamide also has a strong association with hepatotoxic effects. Streptomycin and ethambutol are unlikely contributors to the elevated liver enzymes, as their primary side effects are nephrotoxicity and optic neuritis, respectively.
